name: LED Tail Lights
intro: LED tail lights for utes, trays, trucks, trailers and caravans, including combination, single-function, plug-and-play and trailer lamps.
bodyHtml:
Types of LED tail lights

  • Combination tail lights combine stop, tail and indicator (and often reverse) in one lamp, for trucks, trailers, caravans and ute trays.
  • Trailer tail lights suit boat, box and camper trailers, including fully submersible lamps.
  • Single-function tail lights do one job each, so you can build a custom rear light set-up.
  • Plug-and-play tail lights plug into your vehicle's loom with a vehicle-specific patch lead, with no cutting or splicing.
  • Tail light accessories include brackets, patch leads and adaptor leads.

What to check before you buy

Check the approval stated on each product (ADR approved with a CRN, or ECE approved), the voltage (12V only or 12–24V multivolt), the IP rating and the dimensions against your mounting space. Some vehicles also need load resistors to stop light-failure warnings or fast flashing after an LED upgrade.

Not sure which lamp suits your build? Call the team on (07) 3205 4355, send us a message or visit the showroom at U1/218 Leitchs Road, Brendale QLD.

faqs.question: Are LED tail lights ADR approved?
faqs.answer: Many are, but not all. Each product page lists the approval the manufacturer states, such as ADR approved with a CRN number or ECE approved. Check the specs of the exact lamp, and mount it as the manufacturer describes with reference to ADR 13/00.

faqs.question: Do LED tail lights need load resistors?
faqs.answer: Some vehicles show a light-failure warning or fast indicator flash because LED lamps draw much less current than globes. A load resistor fitted between the lamp's input wires adds that load back. LED Autolamps resistors must be mounted on metal, as they can reach about 170°C.

faqs.question: What is the difference between plug-and-play and hard-wired tail lights?
faqs.answer: Plug-and-play kits use a vehicle-specific patch lead that plugs into the existing tail light loom, with a DT04-6P connector on the lamp side, so no cutting or splicing is needed. Hard-wired lamps have bare wires that are joined to the vehicle or trailer wiring.

faqs.question: Are plug-and-play tail light kits ADR compliant?
faqs.answer: The lamps themselves can be ADR approved, but OzLED notes that plug-and-play patch lead systems fall outside the ADR because of the load resistors built into the harness. Contact the team if you need advice for your vehicle.

name: Plug and Play LED Tail Lights
intro: Plug-and-play tail light kits connect to your ute's existing loom with vehicle-specific patch leads, so there is no cutting or splicing.
bodyHtml:
How plug-and-play tail lights install

Remove your old tail lights, plug the lamp's harness into a vehicle-specific patch lead, then plug the patch lead into your vehicle's wiring loom. Kits include the patch leads for the vehicle you select from the options list, and most include pre-wired load resistors.

The lamps are ADR or ECE approved, but plug-and-play patch lead systems themselves fall outside the ADR because of the load resistors built into the harness.

Not sure which lamp suits your build? Call the team on (07) 3205 4355, send us a message or visit the showroom at U1/218 Leitchs Road, Brendale QLD.

name: Combination Tail Lights
intro: Combination LED tail lights combine stop, tail and indicator, often with reverse and a reflector, in one lamp for trays, trucks, trailers and caravans.
bodyHtml:
Combination LED tail lights put several functions in one housing: stop, tail and indicator, and often reverse and a reflector. They suit trucks, trailers, caravans and ute trays. Popular ranges include the LED Autolamps Maxilamp, 385 and 3854 series, available as single lamps, pairs and plug-and-play kits.

Each product page lists the lamp's approval, voltage, IP rating and dimensions, plus the manufacturer's data sheet. LED Autolamps refers to ADR 13/00 for mounting.

Not sure which lamp suits your build? Call the team on (07) 3205 4355, send us a message or visit the showroom at U1/218 Leitchs Road, Brendale QLD.

faqs.question: What is a combination tail light?
faqs.answer: A combination tail light houses several functions in one lamp, typically stop, tail and indicator, and often reverse and a reflector. They are common on ute trays, trucks, trailers and caravans.

faqs.question: Do combination tail lights come in pairs?
faqs.answer: It depends on the listing. Some lamps are sold individually and others as a twin pack or kit. The product name states 'Single', 'Pair' or 'Twin Pack', so check it before ordering two.

faqs.question: Will 12–24V tail lights work on a 12V ute?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lamps listed as multivolt 12–24V work on both 12V and 24V systems. Lamps listed as 12V only should not be used on a 24V truck.

name: LED Trailer Tail Lights
intro: LED trailer tail lights for box, boat and camper trailers, including submersible lamps and kits with licence plate lights.
bodyHtml:
LED trailer tail lights replace globe lamps on box, boat and camper trailers. For boat trailers, choose lamps described as fully submersible with an IP67 or IP68 rating, such as the LED Autolamps 207 and 210 series.

You'll also need a licence plate light (some trailer lamps include one), a trailer plug that matches your tow vehicle's socket, and reflectors. Plug-in cable kits make wiring longer trailers faster.

Not sure which lamp suits your build? Call the team on (07) 3205 4355, send us a message or visit the showroom at U1/218 Leitchs Road, Brendale QLD.

faqs.question: What lights does a trailer need?
faqs.answer: A trailer generally needs stop, tail and indicator lamps on each side, rear reflectors and a licence plate light, with side and end-outline markers on larger trailers. The exact requirements depend on the trailer's size and class, so check the ADRs and your state registration authority.

faqs.question: Are submersible trailer lights suitable for boat trailers?
faqs.answer: Lamps described as fully submersible, such as the LED Autolamps 207 and 210 series, are designed for boat trailers that are backed into water. Check the IP rating on the product page; IP67 and IP68 lamps are sealed against water.

faqs.question: Which trailer plug do I need?
faqs.answer: Match the plug to the socket on your tow vehicle. Light trailers commonly use a 7-pin flat plug, while caravans and heavier trailers often use 7-pin round or 12-pin connectors.

faqs.question: Are LED light bars road legal?
faqs.answer: Rules vary from state to state, so check your state's requirements before fitting and using one. As a general rule, auxiliary driving lamps may only operate with your high beam, and light bars are often for off-road use only.

faqs.question: What is the difference between spot, flood and combo beams?
faqs.answer: A spot beam is narrow and reaches further down the road, a flood beam spreads light wide and close, and a combo bar mixes spot optics in the centre with flood optics at the ends.

faqs.question: What does an IP68 or IP69K rating mean on a light bar?
faqs.answer: IP68 means the light is dust tight and protected against continuous submersion. IP69K adds protection against high-pressure, high-temperature water jets, such as wash-down.

faqs.question: Should I choose a spot or flood work light?
faqs.answer: Flood beams light a wide area close to the vehicle, such as a tray, campsite or work area. Spot beams throw a narrower beam further away.

faqs.answer: Work lights are designed for lighting a work area while stationary or at low speed, not as road driving lights. Check your state's rules for auxiliary lamps.

name: Plugs & Sockets
intro: Anderson plugs, 12V sockets, trailer plugs and DC connectors.
bodyHtml:
Plugs and sockets connect trailers and accessories to your vehicle. For trailers, match the plug to the socket on your tow vehicle, such as 7-pin flat. For high-current accessories in canopies, campers and caravans, BASE6 Anderson-style flush-mount sockets are rated at 50A.

Not sure which lamp suits your build? Call the team on (07) 3205 4355, send us a message or visit the showroom at U1/218 Leitchs Road, Brendale QLD.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a 7-pin flat and 7-pin round plug?
faqs.answer: Both carry seven circuits for trailer lighting. 7-pin flat is common on light trailers and boat trailers, while 7-pin round is common on caravans and heavier trailers. They are not interchangeable without an adaptor.

faqs.question: What is an Anderson plug used for?
faqs.answer: Anderson-style plugs carry high current, for example to charge a camper battery or power accessories in a canopy or caravan. The BASE6 flush-mount sockets are rated at 50A.

faqs.question: Do I need a 12-pin plug?
faqs.answer: 12-pin plugs are mainly used on caravans that need extra circuits, such as a battery charge line or electric brakes. Match the plug to the socket on your tow vehicle.
